title: Same quality every batch, honest labels, true costs

say: Same quality every batch, honest labels, and true costs.
This is the video for module three of Basic Baking and Snacks Production.
A quality standard is a short description of what good looks, feels and tastes like, so you can check every batch. Most fried-snack faults come from oil that is too cool, or an overcrowded pot.

panel.heading: Three common faults and their fixes

cards.d: Oil too cool or pot overcrowded. Heat oil properly and fry fewer pieces at a time.
Hot or runny filling, or oven too cool. Cool and thicken filling; bake hotter.
Door opened early, too much raising agent, underbaked. Keep the door shut; use a skewer.

say: A soggy meat pie base usually means hot or runny filling. Cool and thicken the filling first.

say: A cake that sinks usually means the door was opened early, or it was underbaked. Keep the door shut and test with a skewer. Change only one cause per batch, and write it down.

say: Before any batch leaves your kitchen, check five things. Even colour. Fully cooked inside. The same size and weight, because customers judge value by size. A taste test. And cooled before packing.

For example, Rukayat in Ilorin finds about one in five chin chin pieces pale inside. She fried bigger batches to save time, so the oil cooled. She sends only the good pieces and explains honestly to the shop.
An allergen can cause a serious reaction in some people, from a rash to difficulty breathing. You cannot see who is allergic, so declare them. Wheat is in all five products.

say: Many sellers work hard and have no money at month end, because gas, oil and packaging are forgotten. For example, Uche costs one batch of chin chin. These are example prices only.
Ingredients, including a share of frying oil, are about 3,100 naira.
Gas for mixing and frying, about 400 naira.
Ten pouches and ten printed labels, about 1,500 naira.
The full batch costs about 5,000 naira. Divided by ten pouches, that is about 500 naira each. She adds 100 naira per pouch to pay herself, so her true cost is about 600 naira.
Her true cost is about 600 naira per pouch.

panel.heading: Cost plus profit, then check the market
items: True cost per pouch: about 600 naira

say: Similar chin chin nearby sells for 800 to 1,000 naira.

say: So 900 naira works. If she sold at 600, she would only be paying herself, with nothing to grow.

items: True cost per pouch: about 600 naira

say: At 900, she makes about 300 naira profit, a margin of about 33%. Shops buy at a lower price, so work out your wholesale price from your true cost first.

panel.rule: Never agree a shop price below your true cost

say: Each week, write four numbers: units sold, waste, profit and repeat customers. After a month you will see which product earns most and where waste eats your money.
Keep business money separate from household money. And when flour goes up, tell regular customers and raise the price. Do not quietly shrink the size.
Your practice: write quality standards for two products, draft a full label, start a four-week shelf-life test, and cost one real batch with retail and wholesale prices.
